output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new vendor rule, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane's rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks password-login requests whose user-agent is 'nettle-http', the library the Android app uses. The first blocks were at 10:41, and the failures began that same minute on every app version. The 6.14 rollout was only 5% of users, and the March security patch made no difference. Quick-unlock is unaffected. About 41,000 blocked installs were real customers; 92% had logged in successfully before. iOS and web were never matched by the rule. Credential-stuffing is not the explanation, and the KPI only counts real app traffic. Do not roll back 6.14, raise bot sensitivity, or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Doing so would hide the problem and block more customers. Next step: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping other protections on. Then confirm in telemetry that Android password success returns to about 96%. Ask Corvane for a testing and notice process for rule changes. Confidence is high.
